questions.problem:
$$
∀{k}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{I}\end{aligned}}\in (0,1),\,{n}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{II}\end{aligned}}+{k}^{2}\ge {k}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{III}\end{aligned}}
$$

Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?
questions.worked_solution:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\text{b})$ or free $(\text{f}).$

- Occurrence I of the variable $k$ is *bound* since it's placed right next to the quantifier $∀:$

$$
∀{k}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in (0,1),\,n+{k}^{2}\ge k
$$

- Occurrence II of the variable $n$ is *free* since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $n.$

- Occurrence III of the variable $k$ is *bound* since it lies within the scope of the quantifier $∀k$ that uses $k:$

$$
∀k\in (0,1),\,\overset{\text{scope of }∀k}{\overset{⏞}{n+{k}^{2}\ge {k}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}}}
$$

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows:

$$
∀\,{k}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in (0,1),\,{n}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{f}\end{aligned}}+{k}^{2}\ge {k}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}
$$

Therefore, the free occurrence is "II only."

$$
(\,∀{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{I}\end{aligned}}\in R,\,0<x<1\,)⇒(\,∃y\in R,\,{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{II}\end{aligned}}=\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{III}\end{aligned}}\,)
$$

Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?
questions.worked_solution:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\text{b})$ or free $(\text{f}).$

- Occurrence I of the variable $x$ is *bound* since it is placed right next to the quantifier $∀:$

$$
(\,∀{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in R,\,0<x<1\,)⇒(\,∃y\in R,\,x=\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,)
$$

- Occurrence II of the variable $x$ is *free* since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $x.$

- Occurrence III of the variable $y$ is *bound* since it lies within the scope of the quantifier $∃y$ that uses $y:$

$$
(\,∀x\in R,\,0<x<1\,)⇒(\,∃y\in R,\,\overset{\text{scope of }∃y}{\overset{⏞}{x=\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}}})
$$

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows:

$$
(\,∀{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in R,\,0<{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}<1\,)⇒(\,∃{y}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in R,\,{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{f}\end{aligned}}=\operatorname{sin}⁡{y}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\,)
$$

Therefore, the free occurrence is "II only."

questions.problem:
Let $p\in Q$ and $q\in Q.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- $∃\,p\in Q,\,2p=-1.$
- The truth set of the predicate $(\,∃\,p\in Q,\,p\cdot q=-1\,)$ is $Q.$
- $∃\,q,p\in Q,\,p\cdot q=-1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the statement 

$$
∃\,q,p\in Q,\,p\cdot q=-1
$$

from option III reads as follows:

$\,$ There exist rationals $q$ and $p,$ such that $p\cdot q=-1.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is true, $2p=-1$ for some rational number $p$ (e.g., for $p=-\frac{1}{2}$).

- Statement II is false. For the predicate

$$
P(q):\,∃\,p\in Q,\,p\cdot q=-1
$$

we note that $P(q)$ is true for some $q\in Q$ and false for others. For example, 

$$
P(0):\,∃\,p\in Q,\,p\cdot 0=-1
$$

is false. However, 

$$
P(1):\,∃\,p\in Q,\,p\cdot 1=-1
$$

is true, since we can take $p=-1.$

- Statement III is true. The sentence 

$$
(\,∃\,q,p\in Q,\,p\cdot q=-1\,)
$$

 
can be written as

$$
∃q\in Q\,(\,{{∃p\in Q,\,p\cdot q=-1}_{⏟}}_{P(q)}\,)
$$

which is true whenever the inner predicate $P(q)$ has a nonempty truth set. And according to the discussion in statement II, this is the case.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
